As we enter a new decade, I wanted to talk about Allies in relation to both racial and LGBT+ communities. In case one is unaware, an Ally is someone who supports a racial or LGBT+ group but is not a part of that community (i.e. someone who supports LGBT+/minority people but aren’t that LGBT+ identity/minority themselves. Honestly, I personally have issues with the word Ally as it implies that supporting racial/LGBT+ communities isn’t the default but since we live in a very racist/sexist/LGBT+-phobic world, I understand the need for it. The label of ally can be comforting as it lets us know that we are not alone and even if we are different, we can support one another.

However, at times, I feel like so-called allies have the potential to overstep in this regard. An ally goes from supporting a voice into overpowering it. And I feel like that can be dangerous. So I feel a need to discuss how to avoid these pitfalls as well as open discussion on the nature of Allies themselves.

As stated above, the biggest thing to avoid is to out speak members of the community when that community is being discussed. We see this in many threads where a group of people talks about their experiences with a topic and will meet resistance by others not part of that community. It is important to realize that as an ally, you do not have the same experiences as someone of another racial/LGBT+ group. For instance, I am Asian Asexual man. I do not have the experiences that women or Latino or trans folk have. That doesn’t mean I cannot empathize but it does mean that I cannot speak on the same level as members in that racial/LGBT+ group. As such, it is important to listen to members of that community and make sure their voices are heard and not drowned out.

Another thing to realize that just because you are an ally, that doesn’t mean you are part of that group. For instance, I am friends with many in the trans community. This does not make myself an authority figure of the community nor does it make me special for allying with trans folk. Sometimes I feel like people forget this.

These were the two bigs ones but this thread is mainly on Ally and making sure we go into the new decade ready to lend our voices to those facing horrible discrimination without risking accidentally silencing those voices instead.
